title: a-tester-run-owns-what-it-started
intention: Every tester run mints a test id, hands it to its subject, and afterwards owns everything carrying it: returns marked with it are matched to the run, its full output goes to the 30-day logs, and any process still carrying it is killed.
why: Akien's re-plan 2026-10-05 (/home/akien/.cairn/foreground-decisions.md 8d, 8e): the tester 'can throw away (to logging) most of what it does. all we need are the results'; a returned testing artifact is the 'got here', and 'the tester would see that it's a returning message, from test abcdefg, and that test can now be marked complete'; the tester kills what the run started. The lived symptom: proof runs leak live processes (two scratch bus servers measured 2026-10-05, one up 2d9h; a cairn-proof-loop unit up since 2026-10-03) and a run's full output is lost past a 20-line tail.
traces_to: Test against live, marked as testing (ruled 2026-09-28; reshaped 2026-10-05: return to sender, tester keeps results and throws the rest to logging, kills what the run started); three retention classes (2026-09-15: test runs past their final result are logging, 30 days, disposable); Law 7 (the record keeps a tail, the log keeps the whole); RULE 1 (everything inside the tester); ticket 71d1bbfa98b0
how: New cairn/devices/tester/runs.py: ENV = CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID, mint_test_id() -> test-<12 hex>, run_dir(test) = address.log_path('tester')/runs/<test> (refuses a test id that is not one path segment), record_return/returns_of over runs/<test>/returns.jsonl, keep_output writing stdout.txt and stderr.txt, kill_what_it_started scanning /proc/*/environ for ENV=<test> (SIGTERM, 2s grace, SIGKILL). TesterDevice.run_proof mints the id, passes it in the subject's environment only (not in the env the measured conditions digest), keeps the full output on both the normal and timeout branches, then records evidence test, killed, returns and run_log. TesterShim.handle_return (the override of the step-3 base hook) writes the return to its test's run log, emits test_returned, posts nothing. Proof cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_run_owns_what_it_started.py, written red 0/5.
falsifier: GREEN when cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_run_owns_what_it_started.py prints five ok lines and exits 0: (1) a run hands its subject CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID, the record's evidence carries the same id under 'test' (test-<12 hex>), two runs never share one, and the id is absent from evidence conditions env; (2) a return-marked envelope delivered to TesterShim is handled, posts nothing, wakes no device, and lands in address.log_path('tester')/runs/<id>/returns.jsonl naming its sender and original verb, and a run minting that id reports it in evidence 'returns'; (3) the run's whole stdout and stderr land in runs/<id>/stdout.txt and stderr.txt while the record's tail stays at most 20 lines; (4) a process the subject started under setsid is dead after the run and named in evidence 'killed'; (5) the same when the subject times out; and cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_tester.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_proof_declares_its_own_time_limit.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_green_over_a_red_under_other_conditions_notifies.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_seal_inside_a_seal_inherits.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_instance_seal.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_green_seal_names_a_tooth.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_first_seal_is_taken_under_the_seal.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_tester_takes_its_reply.py, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_tester_is_reached_only_through_its_interface.py, cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_marked_envelope_goes_back_to_its_sender.py stay green. RED if any fails. Wrong intent if a run must keep processes it started alive past its verdict (then 'killed' becomes a declared keep-list).
watchme: none, because (cairn/devices/tester/device.py run_proof) the killed and returns lists ride every run's own validation record (evidence killed, evidence returns), so the measurement is taken on every seal with no probe; the leak the kill exists for is counted in those records
children: none, because the three files are one component (cairn/devices/tester) with one proof on disk; the systemd-unit carry is a sibling under 71d1bbfa98b0, ticket 2120e74dcf44, not a child of this one

decisions.text: D1: SETTLED: apply exactly the unified diff carried in this ticket's build_patch field (`git apply` from a file holding that text, run in the cairn repo root). It adds cairn/devices/tester/runs.py (mint_test_id, run_dir, record_return, returns_of, keep_output, kill_what_it_started by /proc environ scan for CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID), edits cairn/devices/tester/device.py run_proof (mints the id, passes it only in the subprocess env and never in the env conditions.measure reads, keeps full output, kills and reports after the run) and adds TesterShim.handle_return in cairn/devices/tester/shim.py. D3: SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT: the first seal of the proof (validation committed at 7abaf158) read tooth 1 red — under the seal the outer run's CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID rides the proof's env, the fixture's run_proof copied it into the pinned env, and conditions.measure digested it. Reproduced outside the seal by setting an outer id at 3102a79d; green with it dropped. Fix at 7abaf158: run_proof drops CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID from the pinned env before minting its own. build_patch now carries the whole diff 48f1fc0a..7abaf158 (D1's patch plus this hunk); nothing else changed.

+++ b/cairn/devices/tester/runs.py
@@ -0,0 +1,120 @@
+"""runs — what a tester run owns, keyed by the test id it minted (ticket bf3c16162827).
+
+Akien, 2026-10-05 (/home/akien/.cairn/foreground-decisions.md 8d, 8e): the tester "can throw away
+(to logging) most of what it does. all we need are the results", a returned testing artifact
+completes its test ("the tester would see that it's a returning message, from test abcdefg"),
+and the tester kills what the run started.
+
+One id per run, ``test-<12 hex>``, handed to the subject as ``CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID``. A proof
+marks what it sends with ``testing_mark.mark(<that id>)``. Everything else hangs off the id:
+
+  - the run's log directory, ``address.log_path('tester')/runs/<id>/`` — full stdout and
+    stderr, and every return the shim took for it. The logs tree is forgotten after 30 days by
+    the cairn device's sleep work, so nothing here needs a sweep of its own;
+  - the processes the run started: anything whose environment still carries the id after the
+    subject has exited. The environment survives setsid and a timed-out parent, which a
+    process-group kill does not.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import os
+import re
+import signal
+import time
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from cairn.tools.base.address import log_path
+
+ENV = "CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID"
+_ID = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$")
+_GRACE_S = 2.0
+
+
+def mint_test_id() -> str:
+    return "test-" + os.urandom(6).hex()
+
+
+def run_dir(test: str) -> Path:
+    """The run's log directory. A test id is a path segment, so a malformed one is refused loudly."""
+    if not isinstance(test, str) or not _ID.match(test):
+        raise ValueError(f"a test id is one path segment of [A-Za-z0-9._-]; got {test!r}")
+    return log_path("tester") / "runs" / test
+
+
+def record_return(envelope: dict, test: str) -> dict:
+    """Append one returned artifact to its test's run log; returns the line written."""
+    body = envelope.get("body") or {}
+    line = {"at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"), "test": test,
+            "from": envelope.get("sender"), "return_id": envelope.get("id"),
+            "reply_to": envelope.get("reply_to"), "original_verb": body.get("original_verb"),
+            "original_addressee": body.get("original_addressee")}
+    d = run_dir(test)
+    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    with open(d / "returns.jsonl", "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+        fh.write(json.dumps(line, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
+    return line
+
+
+def returns_of(test: str) -> list[dict]:
+    """Every return the shim has taken for ``test`` so far, oldest first."""
+    path = run_dir(test) / "returns.jsonl"
+    try:
+        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    except FileNotFoundError:
+        return []
+    return [json.loads(x) for x in text.splitlines() if x.strip()]
+
+
+def keep_output(test: str, stdout: str, stderr: str) -> str:
+    """The run's whole output, to logging. Returns the directory it went to."""
+    d = run_dir(test)
+    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    (d / "stdout.txt").write_text(stdout or "", encoding="utf-8")
+    (d / "stderr.txt").write_text(stderr or "", encoding="utf-8")
+    return str(d)
+
+
+def _carrying(test: str) -> list[dict]:
+    tag = f"{ENV}={test}".encode()
+    me = os.getpid()
+    found = []
+    for d in Path("/proc").iterdir():
+        if not d.name.isdigit() or int(d.name) == me:
+            continue
+        try:
+            if tag not in (d / "environ").read_bytes().split(b"\0"):
+                continue
+            cmd = (d / "cmdline").read_bytes().replace(b"\0", b" ").decode(errors="replace").strip()
+            state = (d / "stat").read_text().rsplit(")", 1)[1].split()[0]
+        except (OSError, IndexError):
+            continue          # gone, or another user's: either way not ours to kill
+        if state != "Z":
+            found.append({"pid": int(d.name), "cmdline": cmd[:200]})
+    return found
+
+
+def kill_what_it_started(test: str) -> list[dict]:
+    """SIGTERM every live process still carrying the run's id, SIGKILL what outlives the grace.
+    Returns what was found, each with the signal that ended it (or the error that stopped us)."""
+    found = _carrying(test)
+    for p in found:
+        try:
+            os.kill(p["pid"], signal.SIGTERM)
+            p["signal"] = "TERM"
+        except OSError as exc:
+            p["signal"] = f"none: {exc.strerror}"
+    deadline = time.time() + _GRACE_S
+    left = {p["pid"] for p in found}
+    while left and time.time() < deadline:
+        time.sleep(0.05)
+        left &= {p["pid"] for p in _carrying(test)}
+    for p in found:
+        if p["pid"] in left:
+            try:
+                os.kill(p["pid"], signal.SIGKILL)
+                p["signal"] = "KILL"
+            except OSError as exc:
+                p["signal"] = f"KILL failed: {exc.strerror}"
+    return found
